The Artists

Two Crafts.
One Voice.

Different paths. Same purpose. Antonio brings the words. Alex builds the sound. Obsidian is where they meet.

Antonio

Words / Vocals

Antonio is a Marine Corps veteran and former police officer whose poetry is forged in the space between what he's carried and what he's chosen to become. Writing began as a way to process what words rarely reach — service, struggle, and the daily decision to keep going when everything says otherwise.

A husband and father, Antonio writes with his family as both anchor and audience — every poem shaped by the belief that vulnerability is its own kind of strength. His work moves through identity, legacy, and resilience, turning hard-won lessons into lines meant to reach anyone standing at their own edge.

Where Alex builds the sound, Antonio brings the words — raw, lived-in, and unflinching. Together, they turn survival into something worth listening to.

Alex

Production

Driven by a passion for creating unforgettable tracks, Alex is an up-and-coming music producer from San Antonio, Texas, known for blending infectious melodies, hard-hitting drums, and modern production with timeless musical influences.

Drawing from hip-hop, R&B, pop, and cinematic soundscapes, Alex takes Antonio's words and breathes life into them — building melodies, rhythms, and soundscapes that amplify every message.

Shop Beats on BeatStars →
How It Started

One Conversation.

It wasn't some big planned moment. Alex was over at the house, and the conversation just drifted to music — what we were into, what we'd been listening to. Antonio knew Alex made music, but not really what he did with it.

So he shared a poem. And an idea he'd been carrying for a while — turning his writing into something people could listen to, not just read.

Alex's answer was simple: I love this. Let me put music to it.

The first draft he sent back changed everything. Antonio heard his own words come back to him different — heavier, fuller — and something clicked. That's when they started working together for real.

What they've found, working side by side, is that their stories come from completely different places. Different roads, different circumstances. But the feeling underneath is the same. Pain doesn't care where it came from — hurt is hurt. And that's really why this works: Alex comes at it from somewhere else entirely, and somehow it still lands in the same place.
